name: Renaissance Technologies

summary.text: Renaissance Technologies is a quantitative hedge fund firm founded by James Simons; Robert Mercer was its co-chief executive until 2017. A 2014 Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations report found the firm used 'basket options' sold by Deutsche Bank and Barclays to treat short-term trading profits in its Medallion fund as long-term gains, with estimated tax savings of $6.8 billion. In September 2021 the firm's executives and board members agreed to pay the IRS as much as about $7 billion to settle the dispute.

facts.claim: In July 2014 the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations found that over more than a decade Renaissance used basket options sold by Deutsche Bank and Barclays to shelter some $34 billion of income in its Medallion Fund, cutting the tax rate paid by investors by as much as 20 percentage points, with estimated tax savings of $6.8 billion. The subcommittee said the trades were ordered by the firm's computers and executed by the banks in milliseconds; Renaissance said its use of the options was not driven by tax benefits.

facts.claim: In September 2021 Renaissance CEO Peter Brown told investors in a letter that the firm's executives would pay as much as $7 billion in back taxes, interest and penalties to settle the IRS dispute over Medallion's 2005-2015 trades; the seven individuals who sat on the board during those years, and their spouses, pay tax, interest and penalties, while other Medallion investors pay 80% of additional tax plus interest without penalties. James Simons agreed to an additional $670 million payment.
